scorecards.inningsCommentary: India began their reply under scoreboard pressure, tasked with responding to West Indies's opening innings total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 92 from Rishabh Pant, complemented by a commanding 152-run stand between Rishabh Pant and Ajinkya Rahane that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.41 RPO. West Indies's bowling response was spearheaded by JO Holder (5/54), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 367/10 (106.4 ov), India's innings completed the first-innings exchange (56 Runs (India)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, West Indies sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. SW Ambris anchored the innings with a resolute 38, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. India's bowling response was spearheaded by UT Yadav (4/45), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. West Indies's total of 127/10 (46.1 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

India embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 72 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. PP Shaw anchored the innings with a resolute 33, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. RL Chase (0/14) maintained tight lines for West Indies, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Reaching 75/0 (16.1 ov), India successfully completed a historic fourth-innings pursuit to seal an emphatic victory.

India held their nerve in the fourth-innings chase, reaching the target to seal a famous victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as West Indies posted 311/10 (101.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 367/10 (106.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: UT Yadav (6/88), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, UT Yadav delivered a masterclass for India (2 Runs & 10 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 49%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by JO Holder (71 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by 10 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
